package.anec_layout: 0x1000-byte header, task descriptor at 0x1000, constants at content offset 0x280 for the source-qualified encoder and at align_up(text_bytes, 64) for the Apple-parity encoders, 0x4000-byte tiles
package.manifest: tensors{}, programs[], dispatchPlan[], intermediates[]; bindings carry logical shape, ANEC channel index, physical nchw layout, logicalBytes, allocationBytes, and optional slice {tensor, elementOffset, elementCount, physicalElements}; folded constants appear as constantInputs hex plus binding=constant; shape-only aliases carry aliasOf; chunked matmul results carry accumulation=chunked-fp16
package.buffer_conversion: python3 research/inspect_anec.py PACKAGE --pack-input NAME dense.fp16 --output PATH | --pack-constant NAME --output PATH | --unpack-output NAME PATH --output dense.fp16 (PATH is a directory of program-<i>.<binding>.buffer files when a tensor is sliced across programs; padded lanes are zero-filled and dropped)
package.inspect_anec_limits: the package reader is H13-only. Its operation whitelist now accepts softmax, layer_norm, reduce_sum, reduce_max, reduce_mean and conv alongside the elementwise and matmul families, so the Apple-parity norm packages validate and dry-run; the channel-layout model already handled their dense [1,C,1,1] surfaces. Remaining limit: a plain add on [1,64,8,8] still fails its physical-layout check (research/h13-td-fields.md)

supported_now: add, mul, maximum, minimum, sub, real_div, relu, clip on any positive static fp16 shape (64-lane programs, zero-padded tail); constants folded on the host, sub via negation, real_div via exact reciprocals
matmul and linear with any K and any N: 512-wide reduction chunks summed with add (chunked-fp16), 512-output chunks, zero padding, multiple rows as one program per row

Apple-parity H13 matvec for M in {1,2,8,64} and K,N in {256,512,1024}: Apple's 126-word preparation task plus 157-word compute task, dense [1,1,M,W] surfaces, __DATA/__bss scratch, and the K*N fp16 weight in Apple's packing permutation (research/h13-td-fields.md; oracle cases matmul_m1_k256_n512_ty1 through matmul_m64_k256_n1024_ty1)

Apple-parity H13 softmax, layer_norm, reduce_sum, reduce_max and reduce_mean over 186 templates keyed on (operation, input CHW, reduced-axis mask, keep_dims), with the fp16 exponential and reciprocal lookup tables in the constant section; affine layer_norm is refused because Apple's compiler rejects every affine form in this harness (research/h13-td-fields.md; norm_layer_norm_ax1_1x2048x1x1_affine)
H14/M2 elementwise, unary, scalar-constant and matvec parity backend emitting H14 task streams, ANEC containers and HWX objects (README 'Experimental M2/H14 compilation'; research/h14-td-fields.md)
DAGs with fan-out (residuals, mul(x,x)); reshape, squeeze, expand_dims as zero-program aliases

example: a 768->1024->768 MLP block with relu and residual. The kit's form (two linear ops with BLOBFILE weights and biases, relu, residual add) compiles to 77 programs and 77 task descriptors: 8 matmul, 52 add and 16 maximum through the source-qualified encoder plus the residual add through the oracle-parity encoder, measured 2026-09-06 in receipts/2026-09-05-ane-community/h13-first-run-dryrun.log. An earlier variant of the same block recorded 92 programs in h13-mlp-block-smoke.log; the program count follows how the biases and activations are written, not just the layer shapes
not_claimed: No H13 or H14 program in this repository has executed on an M1 or M2 ANE. Byte parity with Apple's compiler is not device execution; see docs/ane/parity-method.md

Numerical agreement with tools/h13_reference.py is a tolerance, not an equality: Apple evaluates softmax's exponential and reciprocal through fp16 lookup tables, and chunked matmul rounds partial sums between chunks
Geometries off a decoded grid point are refused rather than interpolated; a neighbouring shape is not covered evidence
first_hardware_checks: The ladder is tests/h13_first_run/RUNBOOK.md, eight rungs in order with a stop rule after each: (1) add [1,64,1,1] through the allbilly-derived legacy source-qualified encoder, the descriptor family this driver was validated with; (2) the same add through the Apple-parity encoder, same inputs and same expected bytes, so a rung-2-only failure is descriptor-side; (3) scalar-constant mul by fp16 0.5; (4) Apple-parity matvec K=256 N=512; (5) Apple-parity softmax [1,512,1,1], five linked tasks in one program; (6) a two-program add->mul chain, the intermediate leaving on channel 4 and re-entering on channel 5; (7) runtime-runtime matmul M=K=N=64 with Apple's reversed operand order (y on 5, x on 6); (8) the 768->1024->768 MLP block, 77 programs and 686 libane calls

Each rung records its MIL, deterministic weights and inputs, the tools/h13_reference.py expected output, the exact command, the pass criterion, the libane call sequence tools/h13_run_linux.py will issue, and what a failure there implicates (driver contract, ANEC header, DMA and kernel-bind sizes, descriptor words, surface order, sustained dispatch)

There is no --encoder flag: the encoder follows the operation's form. RUNBOOK.md 'Which encoder a rung gets' records the lowering order and how rung 1 forces the legacy encoder (a matching-shape BLOBFILE constant, which parityPlan refuses because a constant operand must be the inline fp16 0.5, and broadcastPlan refuses for want of a decoded per-channel template at that geometry)
prerequisites_from_peer: Verified ANE-enabled Linux boot with the device-tree node present
Exact driver and libane identities, and confirmation that the loader accepts the 0x1000-byte ANEC header and the channel 4/5/6 binding contract
Explicit hardware handoff for this session

linux_run.preflight: bash tests/h13_first_run/preflight.sh - gates and prints host, kernel, /proc/device-tree/soc/ane@* node with compatible and status, ane module srcversion and parameters, bound platform device with driver and runtime-PM state (must be pinned on), device-node mode and owner, libane branch/commit/dirty/ANEC_HEADER_SIZE (must be 0x1000) with both built artifacts, and this repository's commit and dirty count. Exits 2 on any failure and reaches no device. tests/run_h13_linux_hardware.sh runs the same script and refuses to compile or submit if it fails
linux_run.command: python3 tests/h13_first_run/first_run.py --rung N [--execute] (dry run without --execute; --execute hands the fixture to ANE_CHECKOUT=~/src/omarchy-ane bash tests/run_h13_linux_hardware.sh MIL MODEL_ROOT name=input.fp16 ...)
prerequisites: ~/src/omarchy-ane on branch omarchy (f8df7bc: ANEC payload at 0x1000), libane/libane.a and bindings/python/dylib/libane_python.so built
ane.ko loaded with /dev/accel/accel0 accessible and runtime PM pinned on
verified ANE-enabled boot per homelab-infra docs/jw-m1.md bring-up ladder (~/src/homelab-infra/scripts/jwm1-ane-bringup.sh)
linux_run.first_run: rung 1 of tests/h13_first_run/RUNBOOK.md: a 64-element add whose second operand is a folded BLOBFILE constant, one task descriptor, no ane_bind_kernel, 32 KiB of input surfaces. The runner compares every output with tools/h13_reference.py and fails closed on any manifest or size mismatch before submission
linux_run.pass_criteria: the dry-run plan states them per output in referenceCriteria: byte-for-byte equality with the fp16 reference, except outputs computed from a chunked reduction, which carry |device - reference| <= 0.02 + 0.02 * |reference|. tools/h13_run_linux.py propagates that envelope to consumers, so rung 8's residual add inherits it from the two K=768 reductions
linux_run.teardown: never rmmod and reload ane after a hung submission - the remove path leaks IOVA mappings and the next insmod fails bo_init with iommu_map failed at 0x4000. Reboot, re-run the bring-up ladder, re-run preflight, and restart at the rung that failed. Any result read after a hang is not evidence

macos_run.command: bash tests/run_h13_hardware.sh MIL MODEL_ROOT x=input.fp16 (or make test-h13-hardware ...)
macos_run.prerequisite: an arm64 Mac whose /Library/Caches/com.apple.aned/<build>/InMemoryModelCache is writable by root. On macOS 26.6 (25G83) that directory behaves like a data vault: root cannot stat, list or create entries even with sudo, and the runtime reports ANERuntimeErrorCacheMiss without a cache entry. Two recorded routes, both owner decisions: disable SIP from Recovery on the 26.6 host, or use a build whose cache is provisionable, recorded on macOS 26.3 build 25D125. None of the surveyed 26.6.x hosts (macstudio, laptop, jw14m2, 16m1mbp) is provisionable. Evidence: receipts/2026-09-05-ane-community/m1ultra-runtime-blocker.json, receipts/2026-09-05-ane-community/h13-hwx-macos.log, docs/ane/macos-stack.md
